HOSPITAL NURSE-TO-PATIENT STAFFING RATIOS — INFORMATION SHEET
Prepared for Jordan Lee · Acme General Hospital

ABOUT THIS INFORMATION SHEET
This information sheet describes California Health and Safety Code section 1276.4 — the statute that directs the State Department of Public Health to adopt minimum, specific, and numerical licensed nurse-to-patient staffing ratios for California hospitals, organized by licensed nurse classification and by hospital unit, and that sets out related requirements for nursing-staff orientation and training, rural-hospital waivers, and how these ratios relate to other, separately-sourced nurse-to-patient staffing requirements. It states facts about how section 1276.4 applies to Jordan Lee's work as a licensed nurse at Acme General Hospital. It does not state the specific numerical ratios themselves — the Department of Public Health has adopted those by regulation (Title 22 of the California Code of Regulations) rather than in section 1276.4's own statutory text, and this document does not independently verify that regulatory text. It also does not address the separate health care worker minimum wage requirements of Labor Code section 1182.15, the health care worker whistleblower protections of Health and Safety Code section 1278.5, or general Cal/OSHA workplace safety standards, each of which is addressed elsewhere in this corpus.

THE STATUTORY MANDATE: MINIMUM NUMERICAL NURSE-TO-PATIENT RATIOS
Health and Safety Code section 1276.4, subdivision (a), required the State Department of Public Health to adopt, by January 1, 2002, regulations establishing minimum, specific, and numerical licensed nurse-to-patient ratios, organized by licensed nurse classification and by hospital unit, for health facilities licensed under subdivision (a) or (f) of Health and Safety Code section 1250. Section 1276.4 has since been amended several times; its most recent amendment took effect June 30, 2025.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "By January 1, 2002, the State Department of Public Health shall adopt regulations that establish minimum, specific, and numerical licensed nurse-to-patient ratios by licensed nurse classification and by hospital unit for all health facilities licensed pursuant to subdivision (a) or (f) of Section 1250."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(a) (California Legislative Information text), the January 1, 2002 deadline and mandate to adopt minimum, numerical nurse-to-patient ratios (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)
  "(Amended by Stats. 2025, Ch. 21, Sec. 2. (AB 116) Effective June 30, 2025.)"
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4, amendment history note (California Legislative Information text), the statute's most recent amendment and effective date (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)
  Known gap: Quote verified against Cal. Health & Safety Code section 1276.4, fetched twice, independently, directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two separate curl requests with distinct User-Agent strings (a Mozilla/Macintosh-style UA and a "curl/8.0 GroundtruthResearchBot/1.0" UA), both returning HTTP 200 with byte-identical statutory text for the entire section after whitespace normalization.

A SEPARATE, LATER TIMELINE FOR PSYCHIATRIC-HOSPITAL RATIOS
Section 1276.4 sets a separate, later regulatory timeline for health facilities licensed under subdivision (b) of Health and Safety Code section 1250 — the license category Health and Safety Code section 1250(b) defines as “acute psychiatric hospital.” The Department of Public Health must adopt numerical nurse-to-patient ratio regulations for those facilities no later than July 31, 2027, or one and one-half years after adopting emergency regulations under subdivision (k), whichever is sooner. Subdivision (k) separately required the department to adopt emergency regulations addressing psychiatric-unit staffing no later than January 31, 2026.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "No later than July 31, 2027, or one and one-half years after adoption of emergency regulations pursuant to subdivision (k), whichever is sooner, the State Department of Public Health shall adopt regulations pursuant to the Administrative Procedure Act (Chapter 3.5 (commencing with Section 11340) of Part 1 of Division 3 of Title 2 of the Government Code), as specified in subdivision (k), that establish minimum, specific, and numerical licensed nurse-to-patient ratios for health facilities licensed pursuant to subdivision (b) of Section 1250."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(a) (California Legislative Information text), the July 31, 2027 (or earlier) deadline for subdivision (b)-licensed facilities (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)
  "The department shall adopt emergency regulations pursuant to this subdivision no later than January 31, 2026."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(k)(2) (California Legislative Information text), the January 31, 2026 emergency-regulation deadline (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)
  "“Acute psychiatric hospital” means a health facility having a duly constituted governing body with overall administrative and professional responsibility and an organized medical staff that provides 24-hour inpatient care for persons with mental health disorders or other patients referred to in Division 5 (commencing with Section 5000) or Division 6 (commencing with Section 6000) of the Welfare and Institutions Code, including the following basic services: medical, nursing, rehabilitative, pharmacy, and dietary services."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1250(b) (California Legislative Information text), the statutory definition of the subdivision (b) license category, “acute psychiatric hospital” (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1250.)

Health & Safety Code section 1276.4, fetched twice, independently, directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two separate curl requests with distinct User-Agent strings (a Mozilla/Macintosh-style UA and a "curl/8.0 GroundtruthResearchBot/1.0" UA), both returning HTTP 200 with byte-identical statutory text for the entire section after whitespace normalization. The third citation's source, Health and Safety Code section 1250, was independently fetched and verified the same way — twice, from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov, with two distinct User-Agent strings, both returning HTTP 200 with byte-identical text for the quoted definition.

WHICH HOSPITAL UNITS THE RATIO MANDATE COVERS
For purposes of the ratio-setting mandate in subdivision (a), section 1276.4 defines ‘hospital unit’ by listing the specific units the department's ratio regulations must cover.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "As used in this subdivision, “hospital unit” means a critical care unit, burn unit, labor and delivery room, postanesthesia service area, emergency department, operating room, pediatric unit, step-down/intermediate care unit, specialty care unit, telemetry unit, general medical care unit, subacute care unit, and transitional inpatient care unit."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(a) (California Legislative Information text), the statutory definition of ‘hospital unit’ (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)
  Known gap: Quote verified against Cal. Health & Safety Code section 1276.4, fetched twice, independently, directly from leginfo.legislature.ca.gov using two separate curl requests with distinct User-Agent strings (a Mozilla/Macintosh-style UA and a "curl/8.0 GroundtruthResearchBot/1.0" UA), both returning HTTP 200 with byte-identical statutory text for the entire section after whitespace normalization.

THE RATIOS ARE A FLOOR: ADDITIONAL STAFF BASED ON PATIENT ACUITY
The numerical ratios the department adopts by regulation are a minimum floor, not a ceiling. Subdivision (b) states that these ratios constitute only the minimum number of registered and licensed nurses that must be allocated, and that a hospital must assign additional staff in accordance with a documented patient classification system that accounts for the severity of the patient's illness, the need for specialized equipment and technology, the complexity of clinical judgment involved in the patient's care plan, and the patient's ability for self-care.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "(b) These ratios shall constitute the minimum number of registered and licensed nurses that shall be allocated. Additional staff shall be assigned in accordance with a documented patient classification system for determining nursing care requirements, including the severity of the illness, the need for specialized equipment and technology, the complexity of clinical judgment needed to design, implement, and evaluate the patient care plan and the ability for self-care, and the licensure of the personnel required for care."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(b) (California Legislative Information text), the minimum-floor rule and acuity-based additional-staffing requirement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)

DEFINING A ‘CRITICAL CARE UNIT’
Subdivision (c) separately defines the term ‘critical care unit’ that the statute uses elsewhere, including in the list of hospital units subject to the ratio mandate.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "“Critical care unit” as used in this section means a unit that is established to safeguard and protect patients whose severity of medical conditions requires continuous monitoring, and complex intervention by licensed nurses."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(c) (California Legislative Information text), the statutory definition of ‘critical care unit’ (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)

ORIENTATION AND COMPETENCY REQUIREMENT BEFORE A NURSE IS ASSIGNED TO A UNIT
Subdivisions (d) and (e) impose a staffing-quality requirement distinct from the numerical ratios themselves. Covered health facilities must adopt written policies and procedures for training and orienting nursing staff, and a registered nurse may not be assigned to a nursing unit or clinical area unless that nurse has first received orientation sufficient to provide competent care in that area and has demonstrated current competence in providing care there.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "(d) All health facilities licensed under subdivision (a), (b), or (f) of Section 1250 shall adopt written policies and procedures for training and orientation of nursing staff. (e) No registered nurse shall be assigned to a nursing unit or clinical area unless that nurse has first received orientation in that clinical area sufficient to provide competent care to patients in that area, and has demonstrated current competence in providing care in that area."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(d)-(e) (California Legislative Information text), the orientation, training, and competency-demonstration requirement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)

THE LIMITED WAIVER AVAILABLE TO RURAL GENERAL ACUTE CARE HOSPITALS
Subdivision (g) allows the department to grant waivers of section 1276.4's requirements to rural general acute care hospitals that meet the criteria set out in a separate regulation, Title 22, California Code of Regulations section 70059.1 — but only for waiver requests that do not jeopardize the health, safety, and well-being of affected patients and that are needed for increased operational efficiency.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "Requests for waivers to this section that do not jeopardize the health, safety, and well-being of patients affected and that are needed for increased operational efficiency may be granted by the department to rural general acute care hospitals meeting the criteria set forth in Section 70059.1 of Title 22 of the California Code of Regulations."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(g) (California Legislative Information text), the rural general acute care hospital waiver provision (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)

SCOPE-OF-PRACTICE PROVISIONS CONTROL IN A CONFLICT
Subdivision (h) resolves a potential conflict between section 1276.4 and other law governing nursing practice: if this section conflicts with any provision or regulation defining the scope of nursing practice, the scope-of-practice provisions control.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "In case of conflict between this section and any provision or regulation defining the scope of nursing practice, the scope of practice provisions shall control."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(h) (California Legislative Information text), the rule that scope-of-practice provisions control over section 1276.4 in a conflict (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)

WHAT THE NEW REGULATIONS DO NOT DISPLACE: ICU, NICU, OR, AND STATE HOSPITAL RATIOS
Subdivisions (i) and (j) limit what the department's ratio regulations can displace. The regulations adopted under section 1276.4 augment, rather than replace, existing nurse-to-patient ratios that already exist in regulation or law for intensive care units, neonatal intensive care units, and operating rooms, and they do not replace existing licensed staff-to-patient ratios for hospitals operated by the State Department of State Hospitals.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "The regulations adopted by the department shall augment and not replace existing nurse-to-patient ratios that exist in regulation or law for the intensive care units, the neonatal intensive care units, or the operating room."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(i) (California Legislative Information text), the rule that new regulations augment, not replace, existing ICU/NICU/OR ratios (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)
  "The regulations adopted by the department shall not replace existing licensed staff-to-patient ratios for hospitals operated by the State Department of State Hospitals."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(j) (California Legislative Information text), the carve-out for State Department of State Hospitals staff-to-patient ratios (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)

PSYCHIATRIC-UNIT RATIOS MUST ACCOUNT FOR PATIENTS' SPECIAL NEEDS
Subdivision (k)(1) requires that the regulations the department adopts for health facilities licensed under subdivision (b) of Health and Safety Code section 1250 that are not operated by the State Department of State Hospitals take into account the special needs of the patients served in psychiatric units.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "The regulations adopted by the department for health facilities licensed under subdivision (b) of Section 1250 that are not operated by the State Department of State Hospitals shall take into account the special needs of the patients served in the psychiatric units."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(k)(1) (California Legislative Information text), the requirement that psychiatric-unit ratio regulations account for patients' special needs (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)

A SPECIFIC CONSIDERATION FOR UNIVERSITY OF CALIFORNIA TEACHING HOSPITALS
Subdivision (l) addresses University of California teaching hospitals specifically: the department may take into account their unique nature as educational institutions when setting licensed nurse-to-patient ratios, and the department must coordinate with the Board of Registered Nursing so that staffing ratios remain consistent with Board-approved nursing education requirements.

[Verified — checked 2026-09-10]
  "The department may take into consideration the unique nature of the University of California teaching hospitals as educational institutions when establishing licensed nurse-to-patient ratios. The department shall coordinate with the Board of Registered Nursing to ensure that staffing ratios are consistent with the Board of Registered Nursing approved nursing education requirements."
  — Cal. Health & Saf. Code § 1276.4(l) (California Legislative Information text), the University of California teaching hospital consideration and Board of Registered Nursing coordination requirement (https://leginfo.legislature.ca.gov/faces/codes_displaySection.xhtml?lawCode=HSC&sectionNum=1276.4.)
